articles.title: Websites taken down worldwide as AI reveals critical cyber-security threat | BBC News
articles.titleZh: 随着人工智能揭示严重的网络安全威胁，网站在全球范围内被删除| BBC新闻
articles.summary:
Websites have been taken down worldwide after critical weaknesses were revealed in a programming language which powers much of the internet.  Governments and agencies are urging websites to address the problem immediately. 

The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security experts saying are were the most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered by the technology, which is reshaping the cyber security landscape.

The US National Security Agency issued a warning for organisations to take their systems offline if they are unable to immediately apply a fix, which has now been issued.   The governments of France and Finland were among those ordering shut down of some web services, along with many private organisations around the world.  Japan’s prime minister urged people to check if their publicly accessible websites ran on PHP. 
 
The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz and were part of a program started by the internet firm OpenAI, called Patch the Planet.  They discovered the issue after being given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools, in order to find and fix flaws in web development language.

OpenAi said the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".  The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade.  It’s estimated that around 70% of the internet could be vulnerable to the threat. 

It had been intended to release details of the issue later this month along with a fix, or software patch, or the problem. However details of the flaw were leaked on social media, forcing PHP Foundation to rush out an announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale.

Jane Hill presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Joe Tidy.

Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews

For the latest news download the BBC News app or visit BBC.com/news

articles.readingTextZh:
在一种支持大部分互联网的编程语言暴露出关键弱点后，网站已在全球范围内被删除。

各国政府和机构正在敦促网站立即解决这个问题。

在PHP编程语言中发现了漏洞。

这些漏洞是人工智能发现的，网络安全专家表示，这些漏洞是该技术发现的最严重的漏洞，正在重塑网络安全格局。

美国国家安全局发出警告，如果组织无法立即应用修复程序，请将其系统离线，该修复程序现已发布。

法国和芬兰政府与世界各地的许多私人组织一起下令关闭一些网络服务。

日本首相敦促人们检查其可公开访问的网站是否运行PHP。

这些漏洞是由加利福尼亚州和Wiz公司的网络安全研究人员发现的，是互联网公司OpenAI发起的一个名为Patch the Planet的项目的一部分。

他们在获得人工智能公司高级人工智能工具的访问权限后发现了这个问题，以便发现并修复Web开发语言中的缺陷。

OpenAi表示，这一发现是“近期记忆中最具影响力的安全问题之一”。

十多年来，这些缺陷一直没有被发现。

据估计，大约70%的互联网可能容易受到这种威胁。

articles.title: Is Ukraine being shut out of its own future? | The Global Story
articles.titleZh: 乌克兰是否被排除在自己的未来之外？ |全球故事
articles.summary:
Can Ukraine still rely on America?

More than 80 years after the Yalta conference reshaped post-war Europe, some observers fear a new era of great-power diplomacy could once again shape the continent's future. Reports of a possible meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have prompted questions about what role Ukraine would play in any discussion about ending the war.

The speculation comes amid a sharp deterioration in relations between Washington and Kyiv. From disputes over Starlink access to growing concerns about Trump's outreach to Moscow, Ukrainian officials worry they are losing influence with their most powerful ally. 

At the centre of the debate is a simple question: does Trump see Ukraine as an indispensable partner, or an obstacle to broader deals with Russia? 

The Global Story’s Tristan Redman speaks to Simon Shuster of The Atlantic about the state of the war, the future of US support and why Kyiv is increasingly worried about being left out of the room. 
Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews

For the latest news download the BBC News app or visit BBC.com/news

articles.readingTextZh:
乌克兰还能依靠美国吗？

在雅尔塔会议重塑战后欧洲80多年后，一些观察家担心大国外交的新时代可能再次塑造欧洲大陆的未来。

有关唐纳德•特朗普(Donald Trump)、弗拉基米尔•普京(Vladimir Putin)和习近平(Xi Jinping)可能会晤的报道引发了有关乌克兰将在任何关于结束战争的讨论中发挥什么作用

这一猜测是在华盛顿和基辅之间的关系急剧恶化之际出现的。

从对Starlink访问权的争议到对特朗普与莫斯科接触的日益担忧，乌克兰官员担心他们正在失去与最强大盟友的影响力。

辩论的核心是一个简单的问题：特朗普是否将乌克兰视为不可或缺的伙伴，还是与俄罗斯达成更广泛交易的障碍？

《全球故事》的特里斯坦·雷德曼（ Tristan Redman ）向《大西洋月刊》的西蒙·舒斯特（ Simon Shuster ）讲述了战争的状况、美国支持的未来以及为什么基辅越来越担心被排除在外。

有关最新新闻，请下载BBC新闻应用程序或访问BBC.com/news

articles.title: France promises military support to Saudi Arabia | BBC News
articles.titleZh: 法国承诺向沙特阿拉伯提供军事支持| BBC新闻
articles.summary:
Another of Saudi Arabia's European allies promises military support to the kingdom, as it struggles to contain Houthi strikes.
 
Also in the programme, Russian President Vladimir Putin meets US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, and says he's ready to help resolve the Iran war.
 
And Pakistan's most senior mediator leaves Tehran, after failing to bring Iran and the US closer to an agreement.
